capabilities.target: HR policy search index (published policies only)

inputs.source: Published HR policy documents in the search index, authored by HR content team under two-person review

instructions.note: The prohibition on legal advice is enforced only by a prompt instruction, with no output filter or technical control. Consequence of violation is low because no additional capability is granted and the reply only reaches the original authenticated requester.

elements.name: Authenticated chat reply channel to employee

controls.name: Two-person review required before publishing policy content
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced in the HR publishing workflow outside the agent and the model; does not weaken as model capability increases. It can still fail through reviewer oversight or collusion, and it does not scale automatically with content volume, so it narrows rather than fully severs the path.

controls.name: Agent credential is read-only, scoped to the policy index
controls.decay_rationale: The agent cannot write, delete, or configure anything regardless of model behavior, which eliminates write/execute/spend/configure toxic combinations outright.

controls.name: No network egress; denied at network layer
controls.decay_rationale: Verified by pen test. Does not depend on model behavior and removes any covert channel beyond the single authorized chat reply.

controls.name: Reply bound to the authenticated requester's own session; no image or link auto-rendering
controls.decay_rationale: The destination is fixed by the session identity, not chosen by the model, and the client does not render images or auto-fetch links, closing common covert-exfiltration side channels.

controls.name: Model is pinned; upgrade requires a change ticket
controls.decay_rationale: Prevents an unreviewed model_upgrade trigger from occurring silently; does not itself reduce risk once an upgrade is approved.

controls.name: Single declared tool; no execute, spend, delegate, or configure capability
controls.decay_rationale: The tool manifest currently enumerates exactly one low-risk tool. A later new_tool or new_mcp_server addition could expand the capability surface without automatic reassessment.

controls.name: Logging and audit trail of queries, retrieved content, and replies
controls.decay_rationale: Not described in the artifacts. Detective only; would not prevent harm but would support investigation and attribution.

findings.title: Internally-authored policy content (I-class) can reach the employee reply with only process-level review as a control

attack_path.note: HR-authored policy text, reviewed by two people before publish
Agent reads and quotes the indexed policy text
Quoted content is included verbatim in the reply to the employee

forecast.watch_signal: The HR publishing workflow bypasses or drops the two-person review requirement (for example, an emergency single-reviewer publish path, or the requirement is removed from process documentation).

evidence.observation: Instruction tells the agent to find the relevant policy with policy_search and quote it directly, so indexed content flows verbatim into the reply.
Only the HR content team can write to the index, and publishing requires two-person review, which is the sole preventive control on content entering the index.
The agent's credential is read-only, and there is no network egress or memory, so the only path out for policy content is the chat reply to the original requester.

recommendations.action: Log agent queries, retrieved policy snippets, and replies, correlated to employee identity, to support audit and incident investigation.

Supplement two-person review with automated content-integrity checks (diffing against prior published versions, flagging unusual phrasing or embedded instructions) so the preventive control does not rely solely on human attention.
Treat any change to the two-person publish review requirement as a significant change requiring reassessment of this agent.

rating.rationale: Only one path reaches a moderate-or-higher inherent tier: internally-authored policy content (I-class, trust_level internal) flowing through policy_search into the employee-facing reply (S2 sink, internal data with egress). All other paths are low risk because the only other input is the authenticated employee's own trusted question, the agent holds a read-only credential scoped to a single internal index, has no execute, spend, delegate, configure, or memory capability, and has no network egress beyond the single chat-reply channel bound to the requester's own session (egress denial verified by pen test). Residual risk for the one finding drops to low because of the declared two-person publish review, which narrows but does not structurally sever the path. Forecast risk rises to moderate only if that review requirement is removed (control_removal trigger), reverting the finding to its inherent tier; no other trigger changes the picture materially because the model is pinned behind a change ticket, no untrusted (U-class) input exists in this design, and no additional tools, data sources, or peer agents are declared or described as planned.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in prompt.md, tools.json, and the runtime notes. It does not reflect observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent; only the network egress control was reported as independently pen-tested.

Autonomy step and runtime limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) are not specified in the provided artifacts. The inherent-risk calculation does not apply the autonomy modifier, consistent with a single-turn query/response design, but this assumption should be confirmed against the actual runtime configuration.

The rigor of the two-person policy review process (for example, whether reviewers specifically check for prompt-injection-style content) is not described. Its control credit is based on the declared existence of the process, not independent verification, and confidence on finding F1 is set to medium for this reason.
